blocks.heading: How Big Is India's Creator Economy, Really

items.text: BCG estimated in 2025 that India already has 2-2.5 million monetized creators, and that the wider creator ecosystem influences somewhere between $350-400 billion in consumer spending, money moving through brand deals, commerce-linked content, and platform advertising that did not flow this way a decade ago.

blocks.heading: Economy Has Created Beyond "Being a Creator"

figures.label: Typical Salary Range
figures.source: Sitting on the brand or agency side, this role finds the right creators for a campaign, negotiates rates, manages the relationship, and measures whether a sponsorship actually moved sales or awareness. Reported salary ranges put influencer marketing managers around ₹8-10 lakh a year and social media strategists around ₹9-12 lakh, typically after 3-5 years in marketing, PR, or partnerships work.

items.text: It is the full business layer that has grown around online content, not just the creators posting videos, but the platforms paying them, the brands buying influence, the agencies managing talent, and the tool and payment companies built to serve all of them.
No.

Influencer marketing manager, brand partnerships and talent management roles at agencies, community manager, content operations and video production roles inside brands and media companies, and product or growth roles at creator-tool and payment companies serving creators directly.

blocks.heading: Traditional Companies Are Building In-House Creator Teams

items.text: Speed.
Cost at scale.
Control and consistency.
Strong writing, communication, or negotiation instincts, talent management and brand partnerships run on relationships, not just spreadsheets.
Genuine editing, filming, or design skill you can show through sample work, even if it was built for a small client or a personal project.
Comfort with data, engagement rates, campaign reporting, and platform analytics are now core parts of brand-side and agency-side roles, not extras.
Start inside a small brand or agency, not a big one.
Build one visible case study before you apply.
Learn the reporting side early.
Follow the tool companies, not just the brands.
Turn your case study into a named, priced offer, not a vague pitch.
If you're freelancing into this space, get your first few clients through people, not job boards.
